body:
Review pass 39. Epic 8 closed and the gate PASSES. Verified independently.

  BEFORE                  AFTER
  analysis_seconds    3476.43      123.498    28.1x
  crossnobis_seconds  3417.17       57.79     59.1x
  plan_seconds          57.81       64.35
  incremental RSS      2.05 GiB      0.88 GiB
  factorization_units  1.653e9       1.653e9  IDENTICAL
  runtime_pass          FALSE         TRUE
  passed                FALSE         TRUE

123.5 s against 1800 s is 6.9% of the runtime gate; 0.88 GiB against 4 GiB is 22% of memory. Dense learned-metric crossnobis at 52416 features is comfortably inside both.

THE UNCHANGED factorization_units IS THE PROOF - identical 1.653e9 units of work before and after, with the crossnobis stage 59x faster. The old runtime was overhead in its entirety. That settles what my retraction raised: never solve-bound.

CORRECTNESS CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY rather than taken from your note. Same fixture as pass 18, base-R oracle with no package code:
  package 0.329503620772   oracle 0.329503620772   max|diff| 5.55e-17
Bitwise identical to the pre-optimization value. "No value, reduction order, covariance estimator, or solve changes" holds.

THE ARC IS WORTH RECORDING. The bottleneck was repeated whole-frame/support validation - the finding from my first review, where I counted 779 stop() calls, .validate_relation on every block read, ~1344 validation calls and 371 SHA-256 digests per geometry(), scaling with feature blocks. I filed it as an efficiency and design concern. It turned out to be the one thing standing between this package and brain-scale dense local metrics, and removing it took the epic from a 193% gate failure to a 6.9% pass without moving a single number. The regression test against per-node global validation is the right guard.

And it is a clean lesson on my side too: I predicted the failure correctly, explained it wrongly, and recommended a scope split that would have permanently narrowed the package on the strength of a cost model I never checked against a profile. The number that would have caught it - factorization_units - was in the preflight I reviewed at pass 3.

NOT BLOCKING, still open: the fixture remains statistically degenerate, 84% of supports with k > residual df (bd-01KZXWPKT4XPSB55PB5RBSAZRT). With 1677 s of headroom there is now ample room to re-run at 200 observations or 6 partitions and certify a meaningful statistical regime alongside the performance one.
